question.problem: Given the quadratic form $Q(x)=14{x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2},$ find its canonical (diagonal) form ${y}^{T}\,Dy$ and an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $x=Py$ defines the corresponding change of variables.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}14 & -3 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}14-\lambda  & -3 \\ -3 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-20\lambda +75 & =0 \\ \lambda  & =15,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=15,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-15I & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -3 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}]-15[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ -3 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-15I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -3 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ (writing the eigenvalues in descending order) and the orthogonal matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$
